speaker: leo
text: Today I'm delighted to be joined again by Eve from Club Madeira.

speaker: leo
text: Welcome back Eve!

speaker: eve
text: Happy to be here.

speaker: leo
text: So today I wanted to ask about how you market the Smart Catalogue.

speaker: leo
text: What's your marketing door?

speaker: eve
text: Marketing door?

speaker: eve
text: I'm not sure I follow.

speaker: leo
text: Yes, when I worked in marketing we had a marketing door.

speaker: leo
text: We knew who our customers were because they walked through the marketing door.

speaker: eve
text: That's not how marketing usually works.

speaker: eve
text: Did your marketing door say 'fish and chips' over it?

speaker: leo
text: No.

speaker: eve
text: Car dealership?

speaker: leo
text: Okay.

speaker: leo
text: So how do you do marketing at Club Madeira?

speaker: eve
text: Marketing is about identifying people who will buy your product.

speaker: eve
text: What do you do if the person who walks through your marketing door has no use-case for your product?

speaker: leo
text: Well, I have to sell them something because they came through my marketing door.

speaker: leo
text: I can just make up a new product that they might buy.

speaker: eve
text: Marketing is about identifying people who will buy your product.

speaker: eve
text: If you have to make up a new product to sell to the person who walked through your marketing door, they are -by definition- not in your market.

speaker: leo
text: So who is the market for the Smart Catalogue, and how do you identify them without a marketing door?

speaker: eve
text: Club Madeira operates in three distinct markets.

speaker: eve
text: Clubs, partners and merchants.

speaker: eve
text: Firstly, clubs.

speaker: leo
text: Sorry, why clubs specifically?

speaker: leo
text: Can I not just put a Smart Catalogue on any website?

speaker: eve
text: We are an affiliate marketing company that earns on commission.

speaker: eve
text: Affiliate commissions require high traffic as conversion rates are typically around one percent.

speaker: eve
text: Each Smart Catalogue costs around twenty dollars per month to maintain.

speaker: eve
text: So to have any hope of commercial viability a Smart Catalogue must be on a site with the potential for around twenty sales per month.

speaker: eve
text: At one percent conversion that's two thousand clicks.

speaker: eve
text: Handing out Smart Catalogues to sites without any audience is a loss-making exercise.

speaker: eve
text: Our market is specifically clubs and community groups that have an unmonetised audience and members that will buy because they know their club gets the commission.

speaker: eve
text: A member has a reason to purchase through the Smart Catalogue rather than Amazon.

speaker: eve
text: A customer does not.

speaker: leo
text: But my customer is never going to have two thousand clicks per month.

speaker: leo
text: They don't even have a website yet.

speaker: eve
text: Are they a club?

speaker: eve
text: How many members?

speaker: leo
text: No.

speaker: leo
text: But they walked through the marketing door.

speaker: eve
text: Okay, but without an audience to monetise or any chance of generating that audience, they aren't a Smart Catalogue customer.

speaker: leo
text: You mentioned you had a market for partners.

speaker: leo
text: Can I be a partner so I can give away Smart Catalogues to people who don't have any traffic?

speaker: eve
text: No, because every time you deliberately created an unsuccessful catalogue it would damage Club Madeira's reputation.

speaker: eve
text: We'd need to charge you twenty dollars per website per month to break even.

speaker: eve
text: You'd need to charge twenty times the going rate of one pound just to cover costs.

speaker: eve
text: And the moment you set off building websites in competition with our actual partners, they would refuse to deal with us.

speaker: leo
text: But I can make websites.

speaker: leo
text: Why can't I be a partner?

speaker: eve
text: We are an affiliate marketing company that earns on commission.

speaker: eve
text: Affiliate commissions require high traffic as conversion rates are typically one percent.

speaker: eve
text: Partners are people that manage websites with an audience.

speaker: eve
text: They engage that audience with marketing, SEO and promotion and deliver ongoing technical support.

speaker: eve
text: Do you manage any websites with an unmonetised audience?

speaker: leo
text: No, but...

speaker: eve
text: Can you provide marketing, SEO and promotion and deliver ongoing technical support?

speaker: leo
text: No, but I can make websites.

speaker: eve
text: Anyone with one pound per month and an Ionos account can do that.

speaker: eve
text: The web agencies who will survive are those that drive engagement.

speaker: eve
text: And right now they are looking for ways to differentiate their offering,

speaker: eve
text: for client retention, for billables and for recurring revenue.

speaker: eve
text: For a company in the actual partner market, the Smart Catalogue offers all of that.

speaker: leo
text: Okay, so I'm not in the target market to be a partner.

speaker: leo
text: But what about the guy who walked through my marketing door?

speaker: leo
text: He's giving me buying signals!

speaker: eve
text: Take him to someone who can offer proper partner services.

speaker: eve
text: Tell him to ask for a Smart Catalogue and ask them to contact us.

speaker: eve
text: You have just gained a partner who will now look to see where else they can place the Smart Catalogue.

speaker: eve
text: And with the partner's marketing, SEO and promotion that catalogue might eventually break even.

speaker: leo
text: What if I ignore all that and set up as a partner behind your back anyway?

speaker: eve
text: We'd have to wish you all the best in your future endeavours.

speaker: eve
text: Do you want to hear about the market for merchants?

speaker: leo
text: No, ten thousand products is unrealistic.
